tickCpuP95Ms.why: p95 synchronous cost of one onCarStateUpdate call in jsdom, post-warmup. The DOM-rebuild regression (web-retro 0a32362) measures ~3ms on a dev machine and more on CI; every current app is under 0.75ms. Absolute Node time — no CPU throttle.

mutationsPerTickP95.why: p95 DOM mutation records per tick, post-warmup. In-place updates cost 0-7 records; wholesale innerHTML rebuilds cost 50+. Deterministic — immune to CI timing noise, so it backstops the CPU budgets.

meanProcessCpuPerTickMs.why: Whole-process CPU per post-warmup tick. Charges work deferred to timers/rAF between ticks (React schedulers), which the synchronous per-tick measure cannot see. Startup and mount cost are excluded so the verdict does not depend on run duration.

minSteadySampleRatio.why: Fail closed on truncated runs. Under heavy runner contention the wall-clock deadline can gut the sample base (observed: 50 of 450 steady frames), which makes the percentile budgets meaningless — the gate must not pass on a starved run. Requires at least this fraction of the scheduled post-warmup frames.

warmupMs.why: JIT and layout spikes settle within ~2s. At 20s run the warmup takes 10% of wall-clock instead of 25% — acceptable trade.

defaultDurationMs.why: Compressed scenario hits every code path 2-3x in 20s. With 2s warmup, ~18s of steady frames — enough for stable p95 and covering all event types.
